rationale: P concerns the vehicle state in collision-avoidance situations requiring braking, with its scope linking braking necessity to timely execution. SG-1 and FR-7 establish required braking and its omission as the subject of evaluation. H-1's failure-to-stop-in-time event and FR-7.1 establish that braking-response timing belongs to that subject. The scope does not incorporate sensing, computation, communication, or monitoring mechanisms merely because they influence braking.
determining_elements: “Braking-relevant operational state” is restricted to situations where braking is required to avoid collision, directly connecting P to the evaluation target.
The inclusion of road users and static obstacles is supported by H-1's hazardous event and FR-7.
“Decide whether braking is required and execute it in time” connects the operational situation to the required braking response without specifying internal decision-making mechanisms.
Timely braking is supported by the hazardous event and FR-7.1, rather than inferred solely from obstacle-detection or other supporting-mechanism deadlines.
